topic: Same line in standard form: ratio of constants
problem: The equations (3/4)x+ay=b and (7/6)x+cy=3d describe the same line for all real x and y. What is b/d?

bad.why: Four unknown constants and no data: a regression is unnecessary and leaves the individual constants undetermined.
There is no identity to fit; only the ratio b/d is determined, so a fit returns an arbitrary branch.

algebraFirst.description: Sets (3/4)/(7/6) = b/(3d), cross-multiplies, and simplifies the fractions to get b/d=27/14.

explanationNotes: Explain that 'the same line' means the second equation is the first one multiplied by a single number, so every part scales together, including the constants b and 3d. That number is (7/6)/(3/4)=14/9, so 3d=(14/9)b and b/d=3/(14/9)=27/14.
notes: Paraphrase of Bedrock Prep hard Problem 32, Standard Form - Infinite Solutions. To be the same line the second equation is 14/9 times the first, because (7/6)/(3/4)=14/9. Thus 3d=(14/9)b and b/d=27/14. Explain that both sides, including constants, scale together. Category index: https://www.bedrockprep.com/problems
